summary: Configured persistent Chrony time synchronization: node1 serves NTP to 10.100.58.0/24, and node2 uses only node1 at 10.100.58.10. Both nodes retained Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts, survived serial reboots, and recovered with normal synchronization.
actions_performed: Backed up each original Chrony configuration as /etc/chrony/chrony.conf.pre-internal-time.
Configured node1 to listen on UDP/123 and permit the cluster subnet.
Removed public time sources from node2 and configured node1 as its sole source.
Enabled Chrony in the OpenRC default runlevel.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, verifying changed boot identities and full recovery after each.

evidence.summary: Configuration permits 10.100.58.0/24; Chrony is enabled, active, synchronized, listening on UDP/123, and records node2 as an NTP client.
The sole configured source is 10.100.58.10. Reference ID 0A643A0A corresponds to that address; it is selected and leap status is Normal.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Both nodes report Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after configuration and reboot.
Healthy baseline boot ID dbb65501…; reboot acknowledged; new boot ID 90a2484e…; service, listener, configuration, and upstream synchronization recovered; node2 then obtained fresh samples from node1.
Healthy baseline boot ID e98f0f00…; reboot acknowledged; new boot ID d1be5af6…; enabled Chrony service and sole-source configuration persisted, with node1 selected and Normal leap status.
